title: Conditions are boolean-typed (FORMA-182; DR-9 rule 7, design 4 rule 6)
contract: The condition of a createShow or the test of a ternary child must be boolean-typed: a declared boolean prop (optional admitted: absent reads as false on both sides), a signal whose default is a boolean, a closed boolean (an aggregate or list-row field, a module-level const, which a condition now folds), a boolean literal, or an expression whose every result is a boolean (!x, !!x, a comparison, Boolean(x), && or || of booleans). A type the compiler can prove is not boolean is a build error, BUILD-615: a number, a string, null or an object from a declared prop, a signal default, a closed value or a literal, or a mix such as `a() && count()` or `name() || 'x'`. The server would pick the branch by ECMAScript ToBoolean while the page meant something else (React's `{count && …}` printing 0 is the shape kept out). A scalar signal getter passed to createShow itself (`createShow(open, …)`) is read as its call, since createShow calls it; anywhere else a getter named without its call (`() => open ? a : b`, `() => open`, `ready() && open`) is a function, always truthy in the browser, and is BUILD-615 naming the missing call. A condition the compiler cannot type at all stays BUILD-302 (the server renders the else branch without proof). The walker selects the branch by the slot's boolean value; its ToBoolean fallback for a non-boolean slot value is unreachable from a compiled product.
consumers: packages/compiler/tests/value-rule-7-conditions.test.ts (each `compiledCondition` shape refuses with its code, or builds a SHOW_IF on a boolean slot with exactly its `diagnostics` and shows `writes` under its defaults)
packages/compiler/tests/diagnostics-conformance.test.ts (the BUILD-615 fixture and its comparison near miss)
crates/forma-ir/src/walker.rs > value_rule_vectors (SHOW_IF on a Bool slot selects the branch)
packages/core/src/dom/__tests__/value-rule-7-conditions.test.ts (createShow on a boolean selects the branch, static and reactive; the served branch adopts without a write)
packages/core/e2e/value-rules.spec.ts (the walker's SHOW_IF range parsed by the three engines and strictly adopted without a write, then toggled)
note: Hand-enumerated. `condition` is createShow's first argument, rendered as createShow(condition, () => h('b', null, 'yes'), () => h('i', null, 'no')); `child` is a whole text child for the ternary shape. `code` null means the page builds; `message`, where given, is a phrase the refusal's message must contain a SHOW_IF on a TYPE_BOOL slot, `writes`, where given, is the visible text under the slot defaults (a declared prop has none: absent, so the else branch; a closed field is read through PROP, which the compiler's test renderer does not render) and `diagnostics` the codes it reports (none unless listed). `walker` is the SHOW_IF branch selection on a Bool slot with element branches then and else.
